8 of 20 FAO-1812-2005 2005 (O&M) "169.. Procedure and powers of Claims Tribunals.

"12.. The Registrar General of each High Court is directed instruct all Claims Tribunals in his State to register the reports of accidents received under Section 158(6) of the Act as applications for compensation under Section 166 (4) of the Act and deal with them without 9 of 20 FAO-1812-2005 2005 (O&M) waiting for the filing of claim applications by the injured or by the family of the deceased.
The Registrar General shall ensure that necessary Registers, forms and other support is extended to the Tribunal to give effect to Section 166 (4) of the Act.

13.. For complying with section 166(4) of the Act, the jurisdictional Motor Accident Claims Tribunals shall initiate the following steps :
(a) The Tribunal shall maintain an Institution Register for record the AIRs which are received from the Station ation House Officers of the Police Stations and register them as miscellaneous petitions.
If any private claim petitions are directly filed with reference to an AIR, they should also be recorded in the Register.
(b) The Tribunal shall list the AIRs as miscellaneous cellaneous petitions.

It shall fix a date for preliminary hearing so as to enable the police to notify such date to the victim (family of victim in the event of death) and the owner, driver and insurer of the vehicle involved in the accident.
Once the claimant/s mant/s appear, the miscellaneous application shall be converted to claim petition.
Where a claimant/s file the claim petition even before the receipt of the AIR by the Tribunal, the AIR may be tagged to the claim petition.

(c) The Tribunal shall enquire aand nd satisfy itself that the AIR relates to a real accident and is not the result of any collusion and fabrication of an accident (by any Police Officer - Advocate - Doctor' nexus, which has come to light in several cases).
(d)) The Tribunal shall by a summa summary ry enquiry ascertain the dependent family members/legal heirs.
The jurisdictional police shall also enquire and submit the names of the dependent legal heirs.
(e) The Tribunal shall categorise the claim cases registered, into those where the insurer dispu disputes tes liability and those where the insurer does not dispute the liability.

(f) Wherever the insurer does not dispute the liability under the policy, the Tribunal shall make an endeavour to determine the compensation amount by a summary enquiry or refer the matter to the Lok Adalat for settlement, so as to dispose of the Savitri Devi And Ors vs Jai Narain And Ors on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113705006/

Now, on being enriched through the guided factors given in the Judgment by the Hon'ble Apex Court, this Court examined the issue in detail and finds that some of the factors have been completely ignored by learned Tribunal.

It is an admitted position that the issue before the Court is only to determine the involvement of the vehicle in the said accident and then to assess the entitlement of claimants for just compensation.

As noticed in paragraph No.13, the challan/charge sheet under Section 173 Cr.P.C.(Ex. C1) had been filed on 04.08.2003 for launching prosecution against driver of Car bearing No. DL-8C-1302 DL and subsequent thereto thereto, charges were also framed against respondent NO.1 for committing of offence under Sections 279, 337, 427 and 304A of Indian Penal code and never any order for initiation of the further investigation under Section 173 (8) Cr.P.C. we were ordered by the Court dealing with criminal case against respondent No.1 No.1.
